items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: I remember coming home and putting it next to Coleman Hawkins, putting it next to, bar by bar, next to Coleman Hawkins’ solo and playing through mine, playing through his

ctx.x: I’m not sure if I can phrase this question but I’ll try. If I was to take a solo of yours and transcribe it, and then match what you’re playing against the chord structure and try to justify everything you’re playing by saying “notice how David took the tritone substitution,” and all that, would that be legitimate or are some of the things you do happy accidents?

Happy accidents. That’s a good way to put it. Well let’s put it like this. I remember when they came out with my first transcription of — I had recorded “Body and Soul.” And I remember coming home and putting it next to Coleman Hawkins, putting it next to, bar by bar, next to Coleman Hawkins’ solo and playing through mine, playing through his, playing through mine, playing through his. And then I realized that what I was doing, I mean on a solo like that you could, because in that particular solo I was pretty…
That’s a great answer. I like the way you described it.
